name: visualizations: a genome is the entry the server offered, not an id that looks like one
description: IGV declares `genome` three times under one conditional: a data table for a built-in, a remote json list for IGV's own hosted genomes, and a history dataset. Each case draws its options from a different place, so the name alone does not say what a legal value is, and the value for the hosted list is an entry copied whole. An id is the part of that entry a model already knows, so `{"id": "hg19"}` is the shape invention takes, and viz-igv-second-track accepts it: its settingsContain check reads source.genome.id and a fabricated entry carries exactly that. This grades a key only the resolved entry has. hg19's fastaURL is on the list the plugin names and nowhere in the request, so a config holding it was built from options the server returned, and one holding only an id was not. The user names IGV's hosted list because a person disambiguating between a built-in and a hosted genome would; without that the parameter is declared in more than one case and guessing which is the defect, not the task. Graded on what Galaxy stores: IGV renders an unusable genome and the chat reports success either way.
inputs: In my history "igv genome $run", open tracks.bed in IGV on the hg19 reference from IGV's own hosted genome list, and save it so I can come back to it.
